question.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}-\frac{2x}{15},\, & 1\le x\le 4, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

First, we compute $\text{E}[X]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{1}^{4}x\cdot (\frac{2}{3}-\frac{2x}{15})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}(\frac{2x}{3}-\frac{2{x}^{2}}{15})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-\frac{2{x}^{3}}{45})|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{11}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{1}^{4}{x}^{2}\cdot (\frac{2}{3}-\frac{2x}{15})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}(\frac{2{x}^{2}}{3}-\frac{2{x}^{3}}{15})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{2{x}^{3}}{9}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{30})|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{11}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{11}{2}-{(\frac{11}{5})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{33}{50} \\  & =0.66.\end{aligned}
$$
